text: Toronto hosts thousands of special events each year, including street festivals, farmers’ markets, community celebrations, sports competitions, concerts, and large-scale gatherings that take place across public streets, parks, civic squares, and city facilities. Food is central to many of these special events and is often provided through temporary food premises that operate with limited infrastructure, increasing food safety risks. The continued growth in both the number and size of special events—many of which are concentrated on summer weekends—creates operational challenges for Toronto Public Health (TPH) in conducting timely food safety inspections while also maintaining routine inspection activities across the city. Toronto Public Health developed the Food Safety Management Plan (FSMP), an online planning tool that equips special event organizers (SEOs) with guidance on safe food…

The Board of Health: 1. Directed the Medical Officer of Health to engage other relevant City divisions to incorporate the Food Safety Management Plan into special event permitting processes. 2. Directed the Medical Officer of Health to report back to the Board of Health in Q4 2028 on the progress and outcomes of the implementation of the Food Safety Management Plan.
